chunks: And Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from his father, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abi Basir, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'The similitude of our Order in the Book of Allah is like the owner of the donkey; Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then raised him up.'

key_terms.أَمْرِنَا: Our Order (referring to the authority and status of the Imams)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْحِمَارِ: The owner of the donkey (a Quranic figure who slept for 100 years)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'similitude of our Order' in the Quran according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi cites this hadith to elucidate the concept of the 'Amr' (Divine Order/Authority) of the Ahl al-Bayt, using the Quranic narrative of the sleeper in Surah Al-Kahf as a metaphor for the Imam's prolonged occultation (Ghayba). This comparison highlights how the community may perceive the Imam's absence as a form of spiritual 'death,' yet his authority remains preserved and will be resurrected by Allah's will, ensuring the continuity of divine guidance.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 404 - It is narrated from Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Ja’far Himyari from his father from Yaqub bin Yazid from Ali bin Hakam, from Hammad bin Uthman from Abi Basir that he said:

I heard Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s) say: “The similitude of our Order in the Divine Book is the similitude of the owner of the donkey; Allah made him die for a hundred a years and then raised him up again.”
